lens: Owner and access-sensitive user; overall coherence (simulated AI panel lens)
reason: The inspected implementation forms a coherent local recovery workflow. I traced People account creation through uncertain provider/identity/membership outcomes, restricted incident recording, owner queue guidance, manual remediation and explicit resolution. Unknown acknowledgements preserve accounts; membership failure does not delete access potentially claimed from an allowlist. Queue copy separates recording resolution from repairing accounts, granting access or sending email. Resolution requires an explicit receipt, and failure copy asks the owner to reconcile. The SQL contract restricts incident identity to current same-cycle owners and records idempotent resolution. Applicant materials and review copy accurately distinguish omitted profile fields from identifying original resumes. Desktop/mobile hero captures have clear hierarchy, restrained technical detail and distinct client/student actions consistent with Precision Instrument. Public copy acknowledges pending client approval rather than manufacturing outcomes. No material defect was established in these inspected paths. However, local permission assertions and synthetic button tests do not demonstrate an owner successfully reconciling a real partial Clerk/Supabase account, or a user understanding the privacy boundary. An unqualified world-class or release endorsement exceeds this evidence. This is an independent AI source/evidence review, not observed user success.
notVerified: No staging or hosted integration exists: actual Clerk creation/lookup/deletion, JWT propagation, deployed RPC/RLS and storage behavior were not exercised by this review.

No observed owner journey proves successful reconciliation across provider account, MECG identity and memberships, including other-cycle access and lost acknowledgements. Owner queue evidence is source/SSR; browser tests intercept HTTP in a synthetic button harness.

No human study establishes that applicants understand original-resume identification or owners understand manual remediation. Board resolution of the existing resume policy and privacy retention policy remains outstanding.

No authenticated owner-queue capture establishes its rendered visual craft, keyboard/screen-reader behavior or long-identity wrapping. Supplied hero captures cover only public visual evidence; physical devices, Safari and Firefox remain unverified.

Logs report 673 Node tests, 709 local SQL assertions and eight synthetic provisioning browser cases passing; I read relevant evidence and did not rerun suites or inspect every workflow. Client-approved case-study outcomes remain absent.
